subject: Animation
title: Arcs: Nature's Favorite Path
description: A short lesson to help you apply Arcs: Nature's Favorite Path.

hook.text: Almost all natural movement follows curved paths called arcs. Straight-line motion looks robotic and unnatural.

buildup.text: An arm swings in an arc. A thrown ball follows an arc. Even a head turn traces a subtle curved path.

discovery.text: Disney animators chart arcs on paper, plotting the exact curve each body part must follow across frames.

twist.text: Breaking arcs intentionally — a sudden straight-line snap — creates comedy. Bugs Bunny zips in straight lines.

climax.text: Arcs make animation feel organic. Breaking them makes animation feel cartoony. Both are useful tools.

punchline.text: Nature moves in curves. Robots move in straight lines.

quiz.question: Why do animators use arcs in character movement?
options: Arcs make animation cheaper to produce
Natural movement follows curved paths; straight-line motion looks robotic and unnatural
Arcs are only used in 3D animation
